help.intro: A short text of about 150 words about the German Sunday, which surprises every newcomer: the shops are closed, the law says so, you may not mow the lawn or drill a hole, and at four o'clock the whole country eats cake. The text also explains the one public holiday Germany shares as a nation, 3 October, and why it is on that date. The facts are real and were checked. You need what you have just learnt: the days and months (am Sonntag, im Oktober, am 3. Oktober), the time prepositions am, im, um and von … bis, and negation with nicht and kein (Die Geschäfte sind nicht offen. Es gibt keinen Lärm). Read for the gist, then find one day, time or rule per question.
help.tips[0].text: am + day or date: am Sonntag, am Wochenende, am 3. Oktober (read: am dritten Oktober). im + month or season: im Oktober, im Winter. um + clock time: um sechzehn Uhr, um vier. von … bis for a span: von Montag bis Samstag, von neun bis zwanzig Uhr. No preposition with years: 1990, nicht im 1990.

help.tips[1].title: Saying what is not allowed
help.tips[1].text: Rules in German often come as sentences with nicht or kein: Man darf nicht Rasen mähen. Es gibt keine Post. Die Geschäfte haben nicht geöffnet. Also with verboten (forbidden): Bohren ist am Sonntag verboten. And with Ruhe (quiet): Sonntagsruhe = Sunday quiet, Mittagsruhe = midday quiet, Nachtruhe = night quiet.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: On Sunday you may not drill and not mow the lawn. It is Sunday quiet.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: There is no noise and no post. Only the bakery is open in the morning.
help.tips[1].check.why: die Post is a noun without article here, feminine: keine Post.

help.exam: Short texts about customs, opening hours and holidays with multiple-choice questions are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: No shops, no drilling, no lawnmower, but cake at four: read why the German Sunday is so quiet and what happens on 3 October.
passageTranslation:
You are new in Germany. It is Sunday, and you need milk. You go to the supermarket. But the supermarket is closed. All shops are closed! Only the bakery is open for three hours in the morning, and the petrol station.

That is the law. From Monday to Saturday the shops are open, often from seven to ten in the evening. Not on Sunday. Sunday is a day of rest. You may also not drill, not mow the lawn and not make loud music. That is called Sunday quiet. The neighbours hear everything!

What do Germans do on Sunday? They sleep late, have a long breakfast, go for a walk or make a bike tour. At four o'clock there is coffee and cake. That is almost a ritual.

There are also public holidays. The most important is 3 October, the Day of German Unity. On that day in 1990 East and West Germany became one country again. Since 1990 Germany celebrates every year on 3 October. Then the shops are closed too, no matter which day of the week it is.
